teaser.text: Chubb sells promises that protect people and organizations from losses they could not comfortably pay themselves. Its dollar comes in mainly through premiums, then goes out through claims, operating costs and risk-sharing, while money awaiting payment can earn investment income.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Chubb, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case starts at $10,700M and falls to $10,000M. It then falls to $9,200M as casualty inflation, catastrophes and adverse reserves outweigh savings and investment income. The bull case starts at $11,300M, then reaches $12,400M and $13,600M as pricing improves, catastrophes remain manageable and Life and Benefits grow profitably.

dividend.title: Chubb dividend: payment, coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Chubb pays a growing dividend supported by operating cash flow, while buybacks and capital needs shape what comes next.
dividend.opening: Chubb pays $1.02 per quarter, or $4.08 annually. Its adjusted operating cash flow was $13,906 million in 2025, covering the dividend while leaving cash for buybacks and capital kept in the business.
dividend.closing: The full Chubb memo also explains Chubb’s business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Chubb pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: The current quarterly dividend is $1.02. The base case produces $4.18 per share in October 2027, then $4.38 and $4.58. The bear path gives $4.08, then $4.16 and $4.24. The bull path gives $4.22, then $4.50 and $4.78.
The base repeats a measured annual increase, consistent with dividends rising from $3.18 in 2021 to $3.82 in 2025. The approved 2026 annual dividend is $4.08, but it is not a multi-year commitment.

blocks.heading: Is Chubb’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Cash flow adds another test. Adjusted operating cash flow fell to $13,906 million in 2025 despite higher earnings. The $158 million adverse development in corporate run-off reserves in Q2 2026 shows why older liabilities can still consume capital.

Retained earnings are accumulated accounting profit, not a separate bank account. Chubb must keep capital invested and available because claims can arrive years after premiums are collected. A hurricane can create billions of dollars of losses suddenly, while capital also allows the company to write new policies.

paragraphs.text: In May 2026, Chubb authorized up to $7.5 billion of repurchases. The authorization began July 1 and has no expiration. Shareholders approved an annual dividend of up to $4.08 per share, although the board can choose whether to distribute each installment. Chubb also issued $2.2 billion of debt, with proceeds available for repayment and refinancing. The real question is whether retained capital earns enough to justify keeping it, and whether returned capital was genuinely surplus.

blocks.heading: What has Chubb guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Recent results support the ambition. In the first half of 2026, annualized core ROE and core ROTE were already above management’s thresholds. Annualized means expressing a shorter period as a yearly rate; it does not mean the remaining quarters have been earned. Evan Greenberg also said his outlook for potentially double-digit EPS growth was not guidance, especially as insurance markets softened.

Chubb’s investment and automation plans are meant to support those returns. Private investments are intended to produce substantial annual operating income, including a separate yield from its Strategic Holdings Partnership with investment firm KKR; those amounts should not be added together. Private investments are also planned to become a larger share of the portfolio. Automation is intended to reduce headcount and recurring expenses. A combined ratio measures claims and expenses against earned premiums: below 100% means underwriting profit before investment income.

blocks.heading: What has Chubb's recent results shown?

paragraphs.text: Q2 2026 showed strong operating performance, but the headline numbers benefited from easier comparisons and lower catastrophe losses.

Core operating income rose 14.6% to $2,842 million, while net income fell to $2,854 million. The prior-year quarter contained larger realized investment gains, so reported net income gives a less favorable comparison than recurring operations.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Chubb's next results?

paragraphs.text: Chubb expects to release third-quarter results after the market closes on October 20, 2026, followed by its call the next morning. Investors should listen for changes in pricing, claims and Greenberg’s earnings outlook.
